brief: Nvidia rose from 1% of S&P 500 market cap in December 2022 to 8.5% by May 2026, faster than any of the ten companies that have held the index's largest-company title since 1960, most of which (Cisco, GE, IBM, Altria, AT&T) later declined sharply. Jensen Huang's exit as CEO, announced this week, ends Nvidia's founder-led era; Altimeter's Gerstner and Atreides's Baker wrote the board asking it to leave open the option of his return. Nvidia's valuation has repriced to the cheapest among large AI stocks (PEG 0.2x) after a 13% drop; sell-side targets were cut sharply (Baird -60%) while retail bought the dip. Beyond leadership, Nvidia's share of frontier-lab future compute agreements fell to 39% from over 80% in 2023-2025, as AMD and Google TPUs close the inference-cost gap. Huang was a vocal opponent of China chip restrictions; the pending RASA bill, which would tighten controls on remote Chinese chip access, passed the House but stalled in the Senate, while Nvidia's Singapore-billed revenue share rose from 8% to 22% before it stopped disclosing the figures. A shift in Nvidia's vendor financing could also hurt dependent neoclouds like CoreWeave, though broader AI-demand markers still look healthy.
